Tom — quick answers inline and our proposed numbers. Thanks for the budget guardrail (that helps).

- Quantization: our public pricing sketches treat model family layers consistently; whether you run q8/q4/fp16 impacts runtime cost (compute) but our commitment tiers assume a mix of quantized and fp16 workload. Practically, customers using q4_0 at scale see ~15–30% lower consumption compute costs vs fp16. We will call this out explicitly in the sketch.

- License counting: for hybrid licensing we typically count active clusters. In your case a primary prod cluster + DR that are actively running would be quoted as 2 environments if both are kept warm. If DR is cold/failover only we can offer a reduced standby license credit — we will show both options.

- KMS and integration: KMS integration work (customer KMS onboarding + key rotation policy) is usually part of our Enterprise support bundle. Basic KMS connectivity is included; advanced managed services (migration, custom HSM setups) are billed separately as professional services. We'll mark that clearly in the terms.

Proposed price sketches (ballpark examples for your token bands)
A) Consumption-first (commit tiers, no license):
  - 250M/mo committed: $950 / 1M tokens
  - 500M/mo committed: $760 / 1M tokens
  - 1B/mo committed: $640 / 1M tokens
B) Hybrid (per-active-environment license + discounted consumption):
  - License fee (per active env): $18k/mo (includes Enterprise support, monitoring retention, and security integrations)
  - Consumption rate after license: $420 / 1M tokens (500M+ commit example)
  - Example: 2 prod envs + 1 staging + 2 dev = license subtotal $90k/mo; consumption billed against committed tiers thereafter.

Notes:
- Reserved capacity (dedicated GPUs) can reduce per-1M to as low as ~$350 in large multi-month commits; we'll include an example committed-capacity SLA in the sketch.
- All numbers are draft estimates — final depends on exact environment sizing (GPU class, seq lengths, KV cache usage).
